newsitem.title: USA: Goodyear sues Bridgestone/Firestone on advertising.
newsitem.headline: Goodyear sues Bridgestone/Firestone on advertising.

text.p: Goodyear Tire & Rubber Co. GT.N , the largest U.S. tiremaker, filed a federal lawsuit Tuesday against its largest competitor, Bridgestone Corp.'s Bridgestone/Firestone Inc. unit, charging false advertising and unfair and deceptive trade practices.

The lawsuit alleges Bridgestone/Firestone's two-month-old national promotional campaign for its new FT70c tire uses false and misleading statements regarding its stopping perfomance against Goodyear Aquatred II.

The lawsuit, filed in federal court in Ohio, asks the court to stop Bridgestone/Firestone from falsely representing its tire and asks the court to require Bridgestone/Firestone to undertake corrective advertising.

Akron, Ohio-based Goodyear is also asking that Nashville, Tenn.-based Bridgestone/Firestone, the largest subsidiary of Bridgestone Corp. of Japan, pay damages for any profits or lost sales, injury to reputation, attorney's fees, legal costs and other damages.
Goodyear charged that the advertising uses testing only involving a Ford Motor Co. F.N Crown Victoria driven without antilock breaks at a testing facility selected by Bridgestone/Firestone.
Goodyear also alleged the advertising contains an inadequate, illegible disclaimer apprently designed to warn about the limits of the testing supporting the claims.
But a Bridgestone spokesman said claims made in the campaign for the FT70c, a tire introduced in March, were substantiated by tests at an independent laboratory.
In the tests, Bridgestone/Firestone's tire stopped an average of 12 feet shorter than Goodyear's, the spokesman said.
"We're disappointed that Goodyear chose this action in an attempt to tip the competitive scales in its favor and we expect to prevail in both the case and the market," spokesman Trevor Hoskins said.
The lawsuit comes in the midst of what has become a more competitive, slow-growing, U.S. tire market over the last couple of years, one analyst said.
"Competition's been getting pretty intense over the last couple of years, so they may be paying more attention to" competitor's advertising, said Brian Eisenbarth, an analyst at Collins & Co.
Goodyear stock was up 62.5 cents at $58.625 a share in consolidated afternoon trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
